_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Eritrea covering Aksumite heritage, Italian Eritrea, British administration, Ethiopian federation and annexation, 30-year liberation war, independence 1993, Isaias Afwerki's isolation, and Tigray War involvement.

910.name: Ancient Eritrea and Aksumite Heritage
910.description: Early human settlement along the Red Sea coast; Adulis as major port; integral part of the Aksumite civilisation.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Red Sea Coast Settlements
sub_clusters.description: Early pastoral and fishing communities along the Eritrean coast; stone tool sites; Afroasiatic language origins.

sub_clusters.name: Land of Punt and D'mt Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Eritrean coast as possible Land of Punt; D'mt kingdom (c. 980–400 BC) as proto-Aksumite polity; Yeha temple.

sub_clusters.name: Aksumite Civilisation in Eritrea
sub_clusters.description: Adulis as chief port of Aksum; Christianity reaches Eritrea; Ge'ez script; decline after Islamic expansion.

920.name: Medieval Eritrea: Islam and Isolation
920.description: Islamic expansion along the coast; Dahlak Sultanate; Ottoman control of Massawa; highland Christian communities under Abyssinian influence.

sub_clusters.name: Dahlak Sultanate
sub_clusters.description: Islamic sultanate on Dahlak Archipelago; pearl diving; Red Sea trade; Arabic inscriptions.

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Control of Massawa
sub_clusters.description: Ottoman Empire takes Massawa and coastal strip; Habesh Eyalet; highland communities remain semi-independent.

930.name: Egyptian Interlude and Pre-Colonial Period
930.description: Egyptian Khedivate controls coastal areas; internal Ethiopian power dynamics; European imperial interest grows.

sub_clusters.name: Egyptian Control of the Coast
sub_clusters.description: Egyptian Khedivate administers Massawa and coast; defeats at Ethiopian hands at Gundet (1875) and Gura (1876).

sub_clusters.name: Italian Arrival at Assab
sub_clusters.description: Rubattino Shipping Company purchases Assab 1869; Italian government takes over; sets stage for Colony of Eritrea.

940.name: Italian Eritrea
940.description: Colony of Eritrea formally proclaimed 1890; infrastructure development; racial segregation; springboard for Italian invasion of Ethiopia.

sub_clusters.name: Colony of Eritrea Proclaimed
sub_clusters.description: Italy formally creates Colony of Eritrea 1 January 1890; names it from Mare Erythraeum; defeated at Battle of Adwa 1896.

sub_clusters.name: Italian Colonial Development
sub_clusters.description: Asmara as 'Piccola Roma'; railway, infrastructure, and light industry; racial segregation laws; Eritrean askaris.

sub_clusters.name: Italian East Africa and WWII
sub_clusters.description: Eritrea as base for 1935 invasion of Ethiopia; incorporated into Italian East Africa; British conquest 1941.

940.name: British Administration and Ethiopian Federation
940.description: British Military Administration; UN-mandated federation with Ethiopia; erosion of Eritrean autonomy.

sub_clusters.name: British Military Administration
sub_clusters.description: British administer Eritrea; de-industrialisation; debate over future: independence, partition, or union with Ethiopia.

sub_clusters.name: UN-Mandated Federation with Ethiopia
sub_clusters.description: UN Resolution 390A establishes Eritrean federation with Ethiopia 1952; Haile Selassie progressively dismantles autonomy; annexation 1962.

950.name: Eritrean War of Independence
950.description: Thirty-year armed struggle; ELF then EPLF; one of Africa's longest wars; guerrilla warfare in the highlands.

sub_clusters.name: ELF and Early Armed Struggle
sub_clusters.description: Eritrean Liberation Front (ELF) launches armed struggle 1 September 1961; Hamid Idris Awate fires first shots; Muslim-lowland base.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of the EPLF
sub_clusters.description: Eritrean People's Liberation Front splits from ELF; Isaias Afwerki leads; Nacfa resistance; Derg offensives; self-reliance ideology.

sub_clusters.name: Battle of Afabet and Road to Victory
sub_clusters.description: EPLF victory at Afabet 1988 – 'Stalingrad of the Eritrean struggle'; captures Massawa 1990; liberates Asmara May 1991.

960.name: Independent Eritrea
960.description: Independence referendum 1993; border war with Ethiopia; Isaias Afwerki's authoritarian isolation; Tigray War re-engagement.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Nation-Building
sub_clusters.description: Referendum 24 April 1993 (99.83% yes); Isaias Afwerki president; initial optimism; constitution drafted but never implemented.

sub_clusters.name: Eritrea–Ethiopia Border War
sub_clusters.description: Border war over Badme 1998-2000; estimated 70,000-100,000 killed; Algiers Agreement; EEBC boundary ruling.

sub_clusters.name: Isaias Afwerki's Authoritarian Isolation
sub_clusters.description: Crackdown on dissent September 2001; no elections; indefinite national service; mass emigration; 'Africa's North Korea'.

sub_clusters.name: Eritrea in the Tigray War
sub_clusters.description: Abiy-Isaias peace deal 2018; Eritrean forces enter Tigray War 2020; atrocities; Pretoria Agreement 2022; continued presence.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
